name: בַּרַכְאֵל
summary: Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, father of Elihu, the young man who answered Job and his three friends (Job 32:2, 6). The name is the verb of the root with אֵל, “El blesses” or “El has blessed”; scripture does not explain it. Phoenician names are formed the same way from brk and a god's name.

evidence.note: “The anger of אֱלִיהוּא בֶן־בַּרַכְאֵל הַבּוּזִי of the family of Ram was kindled against Job.”
“Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young in days.”
The verb with El: “blessed be Abram of El Elyon.”

note: The text points the first syllable בַּ (Job 32:2, 6); TIPNR writes בָּרַכְאֵל. Whether the verbal element is a perfect (“El has blessed”) or a form like the Phoenician “Birrek-” names (Krahmalkov p. 127, BRKBʿL) is not settled by the pointing; both readings are given in the gloss. MACULA's Septuagint alignment gives βαραξιηλ.
